pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Add capability to render to a texture
pr_body:
# Objective

Will fix #3377 and #3254

## Solution

Use an enum to represent either a `WindowId` or `Handle<Image>` in place of `Camera::window`.
pr_comments: This looks quite nice to me, and should be very useful. It looks like there's just MSAA support left to add and then this should be ready to merge?

> This looks quite nice to me, and should be very useful. It looks like there's just MSAA support left to add and then this should be ready to merge?

I may leave MSAA for a later PR, because it didn't work on the old renderer and may be significantly more work. I will need MSAA support, so it'll get added eventually.

The missing piece for this PR is a working example in `examples/3d/render_to_texture.rs`, based on `examples/window/multiple_windows.rs`. I've been testing functionality with my own app, and I still have some things in the renderer to fix before I can write the example.

I didn't have any problems getting MSAA working, so that will be in this PR as well:

[![Alt text](https://img.youtube.com/vi/H7dHkMhfCwI/0.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H7dHkMhfCwI)

Overall feedback:
- This is super useful functionality!
- Internals look solid, and I'm happy with the implementation strategy. The way that a `RenderTarget` can be a camera or a `Handle<Image>` is particularly fitting.
- The example needs some changes to its flow to make it easier to follow, and some more explanation targeted at the intermediate user.
- The final API exposed is a bit painfully low-level. I like that users *can* drop down into manipulating the render graph themselves, but I'm not thrilled that they *have to* in order to do this. There's a lot of subtle technical detail in the example, that I worry is going to result in overwhelmed copy-pasting and break whenever we need to change the internals at all.

This PR is probably not the right place to add a higher level API: I'd prefer not to block this functionality, and the PR is big enough already. For now, probably just add more explanation in the example and then we can refactor it later.

If we're adding RenderTargets, is it worth allowing Viewports as well? A WGPU Viewport (see https://docs.rs/wgpu/0.12.0/wgpu/struct.RenderPass.html#method.set_viewport) is a way to limit rendering to a width/height/depth slice of a regular render target.

NB: Not that it's needed for this PR, but it would be another change to the API to add it later...

> If we're adding RenderTargets, is it worth allowing Viewports as well? A WGPU Viewport (see https://docs.rs/wgpu/0.12.0/wgpu/struct.RenderPass.html#method.set_viewport) is a way to limit rendering to a width/height/depth slice of a regular render target.
> 
> NB: Not that it's needed for this PR, but it would be another change to the API to add it later...

I don't think the viewport size be included in the RenderTarget. You might want to clear the entire texture/window, and then write into different viewports with different cameras with the same render target. So it probably belongs either in `Camera` or another component. I think it would be best to have a 1:1 mapping from `RenderTarget`s to chunks of memory that can be rendered to (i.e. they should not overlap) or it will cause problems when clearing.

> The final API exposed is a bit painfully low-level. I like that users _can_ drop down into manipulating the render graph themselves, but I'm not thrilled that they _have to_ in order to do this. There's a lot of subtle technical detail in the example, that I worry is going to result in overwhelmed copy-pasting and break whenever we need to change the internals at all.
> 
> This PR is probably not the right place to add a higher level API: I'd prefer not to block this functionality, and the PR is big enough already. For now, probably just add more explanation in the example and then we can refactor it later.

I agree with this - I think it'll be worth revisiting after 0.6 with some user feedback.
Good point. I agree - why have the hashmap when we could just store the clear color as a member of the thing that needs it?

There is not a one-to-one mapping between cameras and render targets, because there can be multiple cameras per render target, such as the main camera and the UI camera. [(relevant conversation on Discord)](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/743663924229963868/923189739077656646) Render targets are not currently assigned entities, they are tracked as assets for images, and windows are kept in a hash map.

An argument could be made for adding the clear color to `Window`, but only images used as a render target need a clear color. Adding a map to `ClearColor` seemed like the simplest change to allow multiple clear colors, which is required for my application. Furthermore, it has the advantage of making it simple to iterate over render targets to ensure all render targets are cleared.

I thought of keeping a map of render targets to their properties, but currently the only use would be to track the clear color. Creating an entity for each render target doesn't seem useful, and would be cumbersome.
(Added to the milestone so I don't forget to consider this ... it might not make it but id like to include it if possible)

Excited for this PR, will unblock updating my game to Bevy 0.6 (replacing my previous hacky solution).

I can try and contribute an example using this for 2d upscaled rendering as well, if there's interest.
There is another PR that adds upscaling support. #3425
@bevyengine/rendering-team, this is relatively foundational and needs some more reviews. It has two approvals, but I would like another one or two from rendering experts.

Very cool to see render to texture working on the new renderer 👍 

I'm not an expert but two little nits:

1. I find the changes to `ClearColor` a bit odd. It seems like a very roundabout way of getting/setting the clear color for each render target.
   I would have expected the clear color to be a property of each `RenderTarget`. Is there something better about this approach that I'm missing?
2. ~~Is it possible not to clear a render target? I don't think it's an immediate issue if everything is cleared but a lot of the time this ends up being unnessecary, especially in post processing.~~
   Edit: On second thought, if I understand correctly, this "render target" is only meant to be used as the target for a camera - not for subsequent passes. So this point doesn't really apply.

@CptPotato There isn't really a good place to store the clear color per target. Here are the options:

1. In the `Camera`: There can be multiple cameras per target, such as with the UI camera.
2. In the `RenderTarget`: This is a reference to a `Window` or an `Image`, and there can be multiple references.
3. In the `Window`/`Image`: Putting it in the `Window` wouldn't be terrible, although it may have to be generalized to allow for views within a window. But putting it in an `Image` doesn't make much sense.
4. Extending the existing `ClearColor` resource: This is kind of clunky, but keeps everything in the same place with a default, which will work more or less like before for most uses.

That said, in my branch, I've eliminated the clear passes altogether and moved the clear color into `Camera`, because clearing is then done at the start of the 3D/2D/UI passes, and I also needed to control whether depth is cleared for each pass to allow layering. Clearing can be skipped for a pass by setting it to `None`.

This has the disadvantage of requiring the user to understand the ordering of passes, but I don't think there's really a way around that - passes aren't order independent anyway once you give the user control over depth.

Thanks for elaborating!

> That said, in my branch, I've eliminated the clear passes altogether and moved the clear color into `Camera`, because clearing is then done at the start of the 3D/2D/UI passes, and I also needed to control whether depth is cleared for each pass to allow layering. Clearing can be skipped for a pass by setting it to `None`.

This actually sounds like a good alternative to me.

This is great and I think I'd like to merge it as-is because it is small, straightforward, and extremely useful as written. But I do think we need to revisit what a "render target" is conceptually. I think users should be able to utilize render targets to draw to textures (or other windows) without touching the render app / graph (or understanding its underlying structure) at all. 

A RenderTarget should be "an entity created by a user that correlates to a Window or Texture, which by default runs the 'default render graph logic', but specialized for each target". This means everything runs by default (ui, 2d, 3d, user defined passes, post processing, etc). It follows that Cameras cannot own a RenderTarget because more than one camera is required to render the "default behavior". RenderTargets should drive execution of Render Graphs and clear passes, not Cameras / Views. Cameras / Views should correlate to RenderTargets. This also solves the "ClearColor mapping" problem, because we can add a ClearColor component to RenderTargets. This would also solve the weirdness in the `clear_pass.rs` impl which clears based on views instead of "targets".

This does create a number of questions:
1. How will "render target" render ordering be encoded in "main app" worlds? This PR punts that problem to the user in the form of manually defining the render graph. I think we could initially get away with a naive "all non-default targets run first" impl, but ultimately we should be able to support arbitrarily nested targets. (ex: render a scene to a target, which is used in another render target, which is used in the main pass). We could accomplish this in a number of ways, such as using entity hierarchies to define relationships between targets.
2. Some scenarios will require non-default graph configurations. Can we (and should we) let RenderTargets cover those use cases (ex: by adding a `RenderTarget::is_manually_executed` flag)?

I think I'm down to merge this right now so we can start ironing out the various kinks unrelated to user-facing apis (such as per-target lights) and unblock people that need the feature asap. The only change I'd request is a switch to a second `Res<RenderTargetClearColors>` that holds the render target clear color map. That way this PR is a non-breaking change for most users while we sort out the final user-facing ap. I'm going to start experimenting with rephrasing render targets as entities and I'll report back when I have something worth sharing.

I'd like to add another question, which I work on a bit in later PRs:

3. How should users compose "default behaviors" in general? For example, to layer 3D passes by clearing depth, or layering wireframes on top of triangles. It seems like it should be possible without building a new render graph, but `run_sub_graph` isn't enough. Textures are one way to compose passes, so this is related to the other two questions.

@cart one more thought on clear colours - if there are multiple cameras contributing to a render target, is it possible / does it make sense to support a different clear colour per camera which would then clear different parts of the screen?

My current take: I don't think cameras should have clear colors. I think render targets should be decoupled from cameras (and allow multiple cameras mapping to the same render target). _RenderTargets_ should have clear colors. RenderTargets should have a single clear color for the "default render graph". Non-default render target / render graph combos can define their own clear passes (with their own clear color configuation) as it makes sense.

issue_context.title: Add capability to render to textures to the new renderer

## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

The old renderer had the capability to render to texture, and an example of how to do this.

## What solution would you like?

Some way to specify that a camera should render to a texture rather than to a window.

> This happens when a texture is being rendered to and sampled from in the same frame. You need to either double buffer the texture and swap every frame or limit the usage using render layers like here.

Ah, so this is a limitation of wgpu synchronisation? Vulkan and other modern APIs have synchronisation methods to allow waiting for work to be completed so that resources are in known states to then be able to reuse them or so, right? And wgpu has a model for synchronisation that is meant to 'just work' for all the common cases. I guess working around this limitation using double buffering or render layers is fine then. As double-buffering is more complex to implement, using the render layers probably makes sense for the example. I would be good to document the reason though as it's a bit of an unexpected gotcha in my opinion. :) Thanks for explaining @jakobhellermann !
I've documented this in the example.
